note: Life away from the pitch (spec §4 hobbies and minigames, §19 rest and friendship as real choices). Juggling moments are queued by src/training/record.ts when a verified personal best crosses 10, 25 and 50 touches; hobby moments by src/campaign/hobbies.ts at the 3rd and 7th session of the current hobby. Scenes read the facts and never create them. Speakers are the shared cast (parent, friend); tones counted by tools/storyTones.ts. All text is proposal status.

lines.text: Ten. The ball drops and you let it, because you're not going to spoil ten by chasing eleven.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: I counted from the kitchen. That was ten.
The window is open. Of course it was.

choices.label: "Watch — I'll do it again"

response.text: You get six. {parent} claps anyway, which is worse and better at the same time.

choices.label: "It's only ten"

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Last month it was three. Only ten.

lines.text: Twenty-five, and the last five were ugly — knee, shin, a shoulder that shouldn't count. You count it.
Your phone is on the step. {friend}'s record, according to {friend}, is 'like thirty'.

choices.label: Text {friend}: '25. your turn'

response.text: Three dots for a long time. Then: 'video or it didn't happen'.

choices.label: Keep it to yourself for now

response.text: Some numbers are nicer before anyone else knows them.

lines.text: Fifty. You catch it on the way down and stand there holding it like it might argue.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Was that the whole time I was on the phone?
It was. Twenty minutes of the same small thing, over and over, and something in you that used to wobble doesn't.

choices.label: Tell {friend} — this one deserves a video

response.text: 'FIFTY??' Then, a minute later, quieter: 'ok teach me'.

choices.label: "Twenty minutes. Same as last week, and the week before"

response.speaker: parent
response.text: That's the bit I'm proud of. Not the fifty.

lines.text: The sketchbook is on the table when you come down. Open. Not where you left it.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: I wasn't snooping. It was open. The one of the goalposts in the rain is good.

choices.label: Show {parent} the others

response.text: Twenty minutes go by. Nobody mentions soccer once, which is its own kind of rest.

choices.label: Close it and take it upstairs

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Fair enough. It's yours.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: You're always drawing at lunch now. Draw me. Make me look fast.
Half the table is watching. This could go two ways.

choices.label: Draw {friend} — fast, ears and all

response.speaker: friend
response.text: The ears are slander. I'm keeping it.

choices.label: "Not here"

response.speaker: friend
response.text: Later then. I'm holding you to it.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: It's twenty past. That's the third night I've seen the light under the door.
Two chapters left. The dragon has just done the thing you knew it would do.

choices.label: Bookmark it. Tomorrow.

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Thank you. I want to know what the dragon does too, for the record.

choices.label: "Two chapters. Ten minutes."

response.text: It was twenty-five minutes. Training tomorrow will know.

lines.text: The book is face-down on the table when someone from the other end of the team bench sits opposite and says the name of the dragon.
You have never spoken to this teammate about anything but throw-ins.

choices.label: Argue about which book is best until the bell

response.text: You lose the argument and gain a person to sit with. Fair trade.

choices.label: Wave {friend} over instead

response.speaker: friend
response.text: Is this the dragon thing? Can we not.

lines.text: The fourth chord is still the problem. Your fingers know where it is; they just won't all go at once.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: That was nearly it. Through the wall, it was nearly a song.

choices.label: Play it through, badly, with the door open

response.text: {parent} hums the bit you got wrong. Neither of you mentions it.

choices.label: "When it's ready"

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Nothing's ever ready. Play it anyway one day.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: You brought it. You actually brought it to the park.
The ball is under {friend}'s foot and the case is across your knees, and for once the ball waits.

choices.label: Play the song. All four chords.

response.speaker: friend
response.text: That was... a song. That was an actual song. Do it again, I'm filming.

choices.label: Put it down and play the ball instead

response.speaker: friend
response.text: Coward. Fine. First to ten.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Third night this week the screen's still on when I come up. Your teacher sent a note about the reading log.
One more match would take eight minutes. You know exactly how long it would take.

choices.label: Agree a cut-off: off by eight on school nights

immediate.text: Screens off by eight on school nights

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Eight. I'm not going to check. That's the point.

choices.label: "Everyone on the team plays this late"

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Everyone on the team isn't my job. Goodnight.
The reading log is still blank. It won't fill itself.

shared.title: The level everyone is stuck on

lines.text: Half the table is stuck on the same level. You got past it on Tuesday.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Don't say it. Don't say you did it. Fine. Say it.

choices.label: Walk them through it, no gloating

response.text: By the bell there's a plan on a napkin and three people who owe you.

choices.label: Gloat. Just a little.

response.speaker: friend
response.text: Unbelievable. Unbearable. Show me anyway.
